q: Employees use their own cars for work trips and claim mileage. How do I count those emissions?
title: Mileage claims in your own car
short: Trips in an employee's own car for company work go in Scope 3 Category 6, business travel, because the company does not own or operate the car. Use the kilometres from the mileage claims times a per-km factor for that kind of car, or the litres if you reimburse fuel. Commuting to the usual workplace belongs in Category 7.
audience: HR, finance and admin teams processing travel claims

ul: Employee's own car, used for a client visit, site visit or bank trip, paid by mileage: Scope 3 Category 6.
Company-owned or leased car the company runs: Scope 1, from the fuel bought.
Daily travel between home and the usual workplace: Scope 3 Category 7, employee commuting, even if the company pays an allowance.

ol: Distance-based: kilometres claimed times a per-km factor for the car's fuel and size. This is the usual method because claims already record kilometres.
Fuel-based: if you reimburse fuel bills, litres times the fuel factor, such as 2.31 kg CO2 per litre of petrol or 2.68 for diesel (IPCC 2006 defaults).

sections.h: Getting a per-km factor you can defend
p: Divide the fuel factor by a realistic mileage. A petrol car doing 15 km per litre emits about 2.31 / 15 = 0.154 kg CO2 per km. State the mileage you assumed. If claims record the car model, use the model's fuel economy; if not, use one assumption for small cars and one for SUVs and say so.

ul: Date, purpose and kilometres for each trip.
Fuel type: petrol, diesel, CNG or electric. For an electric car, use kWh per km times the grid factor.
Whether the trip was already counted elsewhere, such as a taxi on the same route.

example.title: Worked example: a year of mileage claims
lines: Kilometres claimed for work trips: 18,000 km, all petrol cars
Assumed mileage: 15 km per litre, so 18,000 / 15 = 1,200 litres
Emissions: 1,200 x 2.31 = 2,772 kg CO2, about 2.8 tonnes in Category 6
example.note: The 15 km per litre is an assumption; replace it with the actual fuel economy where you know it.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel bills and invoices and applies IPCC 2006 factors per litre. Mileage claims are spreadsheets rather than invoices, so keep the kilometre log as the evidence for Category 6 and use Senseible for the fuel bills you reimburse.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Scope 3 Standard, Category 6 business travel
